newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower on weak cash, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower on weak cash, technicals.

text.p: Expectations of weakness in cash markets next week knocked CME live cattle futures to lower closes while higher corn futures pushed feeder cattle down and technicals weighed on both pits, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.775 to 0.325 cent per lb lower with August off most at 63.850 cents. Feeder cattle ended down 0.825 to 0.650 with August off most at 80.625 cents.

Packers backed away from the fed cattle as boxed beef values eased and demand for beef slowed which in turn, weighed on live cattle futures. Packers lowered bids for fed cattle by $1 to $62 per cwt, traders said.

Beef prices are seen slipping as holiday demand was complete and the seasonal trend is for beef to weaken. Demand for beef will have to be better than expected the next couple of weeks to support futures, they said.

"We had better have a spectacular movement of beef through the retail pipeline or the cattle market is going to have a long summer, especially with the number of cattle we have on feed and that are going to be finishing out this summer," said Chuck Levitt, livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp.
Technical selling also developed when August worked through early technical support, traders added.

Refco, Paine Webber, Prudential Securities and Cargill Investor Services sold August while locals covered early sales. In live cattle options, commission houses bought August 62 puts early and bought August 64 puts and calls late. Volatility was steady, pit sources said.
Levitt considered the trade in feeder cattle futures to be more technical that fundamental, but noted that higher corn futures also weighed on the market.
"The feeders were more technical than anything else and I think the reason they probably turned down because the corn managed to gain a couple of cents," Levitt said.

Weakness came despite another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index to its highest level in over three years. The CME quoted the latest index up $0.27 at $80.57 per cwt, the highest level since April 19, 1994.
Cargill bought August late after spreading long December live cattle/short August feeders early. RBH and Stone Traders sold, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures closed 0.70 to 2.00 cent per lb higher and said new contract highs in December through April while trimmings ended up 1.00 to unchanged with August and February setting new highs.
August boneless beef was up the least at 94.70 cents and August trimmings were up most in that pit at 44.00 cents.
Commercial interest was cited in both pits despite the weaker undertone to beef prices, floor sources said.
